text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Hundreds of demonstrators were detained. The government sealed the city with thousands of policemen and soldiers. People were trapped in traffic jams.
-Parliamentary committees begin on Monday debating 1997 state budget.
-Lebanon and France signed an economic agreement to promote investments.
-A demonstration in Barbour-Noueiri breaks the ban. Security forces suppress journalists amid unjustified panic.
-The Beirut Stock Exchange told 38 companies listed before it shut down during the civil war to meet listing requirements by December 21 or be crossed out.
-Solidere Global Depositary Receipts (GDR) issue falls short of target and prices were $11.60/70.
-A German delegation discussed with the prosecutor general means to take back to Germany tonnes of polluted plastic waste.
-Solidere shares fell on the Beirut Stock Exchange a day after the company made a $77-million GDR issue.
-Lebanon's total debt at 17,700 billion Lebanese pounds at the end of September.
